title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp-plain: six-class (negation + GLV) parallel Pollard rho in G1 with truncated-product canonicalisation

claims.statement: For a uniform challenge T=[x]P0 in BLS12-381 G1 (x uniform in 0..r-1; T=infinity returns x=0), the algorithm in proof.md recovers and outputs the scalar x with success probability at least 0.40 using at most 2^126.41 total batched-incomplete-affine-G1-addition equivalents (C=2,000 scalar AArch64 instructions per unit). The algorithm is parallel distinguished-point Pollard rho (van Oorschot-Wiener; M=2^20 walks; distinguished probability 2^-64 from limb 1 of the class key; trail cap 20*2^64 operations; fresh trail after every distinguished class) on the N=(r-1)/6 orbits of G1 under the order-6 automorphism group generated by negation and phi(x,y)=(beta*x,y)=[lambda] (lambda=0xac45a4010001a40200000000ffffffff). The class key is |y|=min(y,p-y); the twist index of the canonical member (min over beta^j x) is decided exactly from a truncated 23-multiply fixed-point product of x by floor(2^448*beta/p) with an exact one-Fp-multiplication fallback on near-ties (proof.md section 2.1); an R=2048 twisted multiplier table makes every ordinary step exactly one batched affine G1 addition plus at most 240 other instructions (the rare exact fallback of section 2.1 and inversions of batches smaller than 2^15 are separately metered actions). 2-cycles and cycles of length <=64 are detected with 192-bit key fingerprints and escaped deterministically by doubling the minimum-key class of the cycle; exceptional additions abandon the trail. Every action (preprocessing, random words, rejection-sampling attempts, trail starts and redraws, steps, doublings, cycle traversals, reports, hash probes, table initialisation, re-walks, solving, verification, output) is charged at an upper-bound price to a global work meter before execution and the attack halts with failure if the meter would exceed W_max=2^126.41, so total work is at most 2^126.41 on every run. Phase 1 runs until the step part of the meter reaches 1.12*S_ops=2^126.4023 units (S_ops=1.06*S0/0.998, S0=sqrt(2N'ln(1/0.6)), N'=N*2048/2047); phase 2 only completes open trails; report-table capacity (2^63.25 records) and match count (8) are caps whose violation is counted as failure; early halting of the meter has probability below 2^-43. Trail coefficients are fresh uniform pairs stored in full; on a key match both trails are re-walked with coefficients reduced mod r after every operation and x=(e_2-e_1)/(f_1-f_2) mod r (canonical coefficients e, f) is verified by [x]P0=T before output. The meter covers the table (preprocessing below 2^24 units), all trail starts, phase 2, report storage, hash-table initialisation and lookup, re-walks, escapes, failures and verification. Peak memory is below 2^72 bytes; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. The success bound relies on heuristic H1: the first inter-trail class collision obeys the random-mapping law with the Brent-Pollard R/(R-1) correction and an allowance of 5% slowdown in collision time at the budget quantile (kappa=1.05; P(first collision within 1.06*S0 fresh visits) >=0.4058), and the partition/distinguished bits of |y| behave pseudo-randomly; beta*x mod p is assumed equidistributed along the walk, which only affects the rate of metered section-2.1 fallbacks and hence the early-halt probability, never correctness or the work bound; fruitless-cycle waste and doubling rates concentrate at their expected values (deviations counted as failure, negligible probability). H1 is supported by toy-curve experiments, including a no-automorphism control; no production-size run is claimed.

experiments.purpose: Part A: on BLS12-381 G1 itself, check the GLV pair (beta, lambda), orbit size 6 and unit action, |y| class key, canonical-member rule, the truncated-product canonical-index rule of section 2.1 against the exact rule (random and adversarial near-tie production inputs), twisted-table step identity, doubling as a class map, twisted table entries, coefficient tracking along production walk steps, and the collision-solving formula and its sign on two production trails forced to merge. Part B: run the complete per-trail algorithm of proof.md (canonical rule, twisted table, 2-cycle and checkpoint escapes, trail cap, exceptional-addition abandonment, distinguished classes, restarts, re-walk solving, verification) on the prime-order subgroup of a toy curve y^2=x^3+4 over F_q and report the number of class visits to the first inter-trail collision against the random-mapping model, plus measured fruitless-cycle rates; with pipeline=true it also applies the production resource rules scaled to the toy (phase-1 budget 1.06*S0/0.998 in class visits, phase 2, report capacity, 8-match cap) and reports the success rate. Optional classes=1 or 2 runs a control walk without the GLV (or without any) automorphism. Toy scale only; does not validate production costs.
